findings.issue_text: [BUG] The `<%- end if %>` tag does not close the if/else — it emits the raw Ruby fragment `end if;` into the compiled template (the Erubis handler terminates `<% %>` chunks with a semicolon), which is a SyntaxError. Compiling best.html.erb raises ActionView::Template::Error, so every /embed/best request for an embed_url that already has a topic returns a 500 instead of the embed page; the new controller specs never compile views, so CI stays green while the feature is dead in production.

[BUG] `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references a bundle that is never registered for precompilation — the diff adds app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and app/assets/javascripts/embed.js but adds no 'embed' entry to any asset precompile list. In production, where assets are precompiled and digested, every /embed/best request (both the topic view and the loading view render this layout) raises AssetNotPrecompiledError ("embed.css isn't precompiled") and returns a 500, and embedding sites cannot fetch embed.js either; it appears to work only in development where Sprockets compiles on demand.

[BUG] ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is regenerated — the repo's default Gemfile.lock (the Rails 3.2 track that the '_rails4' suffix exists to parallel) is left without either gem. Any frozen or deployment-mode `bundle install` on the default track aborts with 'Your Gemfile.lock is out of date', and a plain `bundle install` silently rewrites the committed lockfile, so the non-rails4 CI/deploy track cannot install the gems the new poll_feed/topic_embed code requires.

[ADVISORY] The PR edits the already-released CreateTopTopics migration to add `force: true`, so create_table now issues a DROP TABLE before creating. Environments that already ran this migration never see the edit, and an operator running `rake db:migrate:redo` (or rollback then migrate) on any environment silently drops the top_topics table and its data; the flag only papers over the author's local dev database.

[ADVISORY] The new PollFeed job's core behavior — fetching the feed, the link/id URL fallback, unescaping item content, and delegating to TopicEmbed.import — has no test anywhere in the diff (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only exercises the enable/disable guards). A regression in the item loop silently stops RSS/Atom importing — the job runs hourly with retry: false and no spec fails — and operators discover it only when embedded topics stop appearing.

[BUG] The header if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, a malformed ERB terminator that compiles to `end if;` (the ERB engine joins each statement with a semicolon), which is a Ruby syntax error rather than the plain `end` the block requires. ActionView fails to compile best.html.erb on first render, so every /embed/best request that finds a topic returns a 500 instead of the comment list — the feature's primary success path is dead, and no spec in the diff renders the template to catch it.

[BUG] PollFeed passes raw RSS item content into TopicEmbed.import, which stores it with cook_method raw_html so Post#cook returns it verbatim — feed HTML is never sanitized, because the readability tag whitelist is applied only on the sibling import_remote path. A compromised or third-party-aggregating feed injects arbitrary <script> HTML that is stored as post.cooked and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed iframe and in the normal topic view, executing on the Discourse origin for every viewer — stored XSS and session hijack.

[BUG] import_remote passes doc.content into import with no nil check, and import's first statement is `contents << ...`, so any page where readability extracts no article (non-HTML URL, empty body) crashes with NoMethodError on nil. The RetrieveTopic job for that embed_url fails on every attempt, no TopicEmbed row is ever created, and the blog page's iframe shows 'Loading Discussion...' and reloads every 30 seconds forever with no error shown to the reader.

[BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item error handling, and two crash triggers pass the existing guards: an item without content (`nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError) and a link that satisfies import's `^https?\://` regex but fails URI parsing inside absolutize_urls (URI::InvalidURIError, e.g. a space in the path). One malformed feed item aborts the entire import at that point, and because items are processed in order with retry disabled, every feed item after it is never imported on any future hourly run — feed polling is permanently stuck.

[BUG] absolutize_urls rewrites any href/src starting with '/', so protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/img.jpg have their leading slashes stripped by `sub(/^\/+/, '')` and are rebuilt as http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg, while bare-relative links (page.html) are left untouched. Imported articles using protocol-relative CDN assets or non-root-relative links render with broken images and links pointing at nonexistent paths on the wrong host — the embedded content is visibly corrupted.

[BUG] The imported_from footer interpolates url directly into an HTML attribute (`<a href='#{url}'>`) inside raw-HTML-cooked content with no escaping, and url is only regex-checked (`^https?://`), never attribute-escaped. A feed item link like http://x.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) (quotes and equals signs are legal URI path characters, so the embed_url path passes URI parsing too) breaks out of the href attribute, yielding stored attribute-injection XSS rendered raw in the embed and topic view — unsanitized even when the article body went through the readability whitelist.

[BUG] The readability whitelist keeps a[href] and img[src] values verbatim with no URL scheme filtering, and absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs starting with '/', so javascript: URLs survive import intact. An embedded page containing <a href='javascript:...'> imports a clickable javascript: link that renders raw in the Discourse-origin iframe, executing script on the Discourse origin when a reader clicks it.

[BUG] import_remote fetches with open(url), which follows HTTP redirects, and only the initial embed_url host is validated against embeddable_host — the final URL after redirection is never re-checked. Any redirect on the embeddable host (open redirect, link shortener) turns the background job into an SSRF fetch of internal URLs (cloud metadata endpoints, admin panels), and the retrieved content is imported as a publicly viewable topic.

[BUG] The disqus import was rewritten to call TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link]) instead of creating posts directly: the documented -c/--category option was deleted (thor errors on unknown options), threads whose link is not http(s) are silently skipped because import returns nil, and the first unreachable link raises inside open() and aborts the whole import mid-run. Operators running the previously documented `disqus import -c <category>` invocation get an unknown-option error, and anyone importing an export containing one dead or non-http link gets a partial, silently incomplete import with no report of which threads were dropped.

[BUG] t[:link] from the disqus export file is passed straight into open() with no validation (import_remote applies no regex or URI check before opening), and Kernel#open executes strings beginning with '|' as shell commands. Importing a disqus export received from a third party whose thread link field is '| <command>' executes that command on the operator's machine during the thor task — arbitrary command execution from an untrusted input file.

[ADVISORY] topic_id_for_embed matches embed_url by exact string comparison with no normalization, while the two producers of that string — the feed's i.link and the embedding page's discourseEmbedUrl — are independent and routinely differ (trailing slash, query params). When they differ, the hourly poll imports the article under the feed link and the retriever imports it again under the page URL, creating duplicate topics; the embed displays the retriever's copy, so later feed revisions update a topic the embed never shows.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed rows have no deletion path anywhere in the diff (no destroy callback on Topic/Post, no admin UI or API), and perform_retrieve treats row existence as authoritative (`return if TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?`). When staff delete an embedded topic (e.g. spam), the orphaned row makes that blog page's embed fail forever and permanently blocks re-import — recovery requires direct database surgery, since nothing in the product can remove the row.

[ADVISORY] The embed flow has exactly two states — topic found, or 'loading' with a 30-second reload — and no terminal error state for retrieval that can never succeed. Every permanent failure mode in this diff (nil extracted content, oversized embed_url, malformed feed link) leaves each visitor's browser reloading the iframe every 30 seconds and the server re-enqueuing RetrieveTopic every 60 seconds indefinitely, with the reader never told that anything failed.

[ADVISORY] Every unauthenticated /embed/best request with an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and the only gates — the Referer header check and the per-URL 60-second redis throttle — are both bypassable (referer is a client-spoofable header; the throttle is per-URL, so distinct URLs each get a fresh slot). A script hammering the endpoint with distinct embed_url values and a forged Referer makes the Discourse server create an unbounded number of topics under embed_by_username and fetch an unbounded number of pages from the partner host — unauthenticated topic-spam and outbound-fetch amplification.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined and never called anywhere in the diff — the conditional-polling/change-detection mechanism it names was silently dropped from the implementation. The job re-fetches and re-parses the entire feed and re-processes every item every hour forever, and the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing change detection exists.

[ADVISORY] The controller spec mocks TopicView.new and controller specs do not render templates, so none of the three new ERB files (best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb) is ever compiled or executed by any test in the diff. Template-level defects — including the `end if` terminator in best.html.erb and the `raw post.cooked` rendering — ship with a green suite; the first execution of these templates happens in production.

[ADVISORY] The client half of the feature — the postMessage origin check and the discourse-resize height handshake — is new non-trivial logic with no test anywhere in the diff (no spec/javascripts additions). A regression in the origin check or the resize payload silently breaks every embedding site at once (frozen or zero-height iframes), and nothing in CI notices.

[ADVISORY] ruby-readability and simple-rss were added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock was regenerated — the base Gemfile.lock implied by the _rails4 suffix is left without the two new gems. Any build or deploy bundling against the non-rails4 lockfile fails (bundle --deployment: missing gems) or runs without them and crashes at the first require 'simple-rss' inside the scheduled job.

[BUG] embed_url is created as a default-limit 255-character string column, and TopicEmbed.create! inserts the full embed URL with no length check. Canonical URLs longer than 255 characters (UTM-heavy permalinks are common) make create! raise inside the RetrieveTopic job, so those articles never get a topic and their embeds sit in the infinite loading-reload loop.

[ADVISORY] embeddable_host is compared verbatim against URI(referer).host with no normalization or format validation of the setting itself. An operator who enters 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'eviltrout.com/' in the setting (the description only says 'Host') silently 403s every embed request, and the failure is invisible because it happens inside an iframe with no feedback anywhere.

[ADVISORY] The new raw_html branch of Post#cook returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins registered on that filter silently never run on imported posts. Plugin authors whose after_post_cook hooks transform or sanitize cooked HTML are silently bypassed by exactly the posts carrying unsanitized external feed HTML — a site relying on such a plugin for HTML policy has raw feed content rendered unfiltered.

[BUG] The fragment `<%- end if %>` compiles to a bare `end if` with no condition on the generated line (the next generated line is the following output statement), which is a Ruby syntax error, so best.html.erb fails to compile. Every request to /embed/best for a URL that already has a topic raises ActionView::SyntaxError and returns a 500 instead of the comment list, so the embed widget permanently breaks after the first successful background retrieval; no spec catches it because the controller specs never render views.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores externally supplied feed/scraped content with cook_method raw_html, which Post#cook returns verbatim with no sanitization, and best.html.erb renders it via `raw post.cooked`. Any HTML in an imported item executes as script on the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embed iframe and the imported topic — PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight through, which even expands <script> entities into live tags — giving a single malicious feed item stored XSS on the forum.

[BUG] The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into the imported_from footer (single-quoted href and bare text node) even though the only validation is the ^https?:// prefix check, so quotes and angle brackets pass through. A feed item link such as http://host/1'><script>alert(1)</script> injects markup into every rendered copy of the post (cooked is emitted raw), giving the feed author a second, independent stored-XSS path into the Discourse origin.

[BUG] poll_feed dereferences i.content with no nil guard, but items in description-only RSS 2.0 feeds — the format the feed_polling_url setting explicitly advertises — have no content element, so SimpleRSS yields nil and the poll crashes with NoMethodError. The hourly poll dies before importing anything, and because the job declares sidekiq_options retry: false the exception is discarded silently, so feed importing stops with no error surfaced to the operator.

[ADVISORY] The PR rewrites the unrelated Disqus importer to route through TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently deleting the documented -c/--category option, dropping created_at preservation, and adding an unguarded network fetch of every thread link. Operators whose import scripts pass -c now fail (Thor rejects the unknown option) and every imported topic lands in uncategorized with today's timestamp instead of the thread's original date; a single dead link in the export raises OpenURI::HTTPError inside the threads loop and aborts the whole import mid-run with no resume — none of which the embed requirement asks for.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads the iframe unconditionally every 30 seconds with no retry cap and no error state, while the retrieval it waits on can fail permanently (embed_by_username blank, embed_url host differing from embeddable_host, fetch errors). A misconfigured embed — the most likely first-run state — shows visitors an eternal 'Loading Discussion...' widget that re-requests /embed/best and re-enqueues a RetrieveTopic job every 30 seconds per visitor, with nothing at the point of failure telling the operator why.

[ADVISORY] The referer host check is the only gate on the unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint, but Referer is a client-supplied header, and the Jobs.enqueue at line 15 runs on every request with no request-level rate limit. Anyone can curl the endpoint with a forged Referer and unlimited distinct embed_url values to flood the sidekiq queue with RetrieveTopic jobs, each performing redis operations and — once past the per-URL 60-second key — an outbound HTTP fetch against the configured host, turning the forum into an unauthenticated job-flooding and request-amplification vector.

[ADVISORY] The new specs cover only the settings gating and stub out the behavior the feature actually adds — poll_feed's URL fallback, entity unescaping and TopicEmbed.import call, plus TopicEmbed.import_remote and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/fetch_http, have zero coverage. A regression in the feed import loop (such as the nil-content crash or an escaping change) breaks feed importing with no failing spec, and because the job is scheduled with retry: false nothing in CI or production surfaces it until operators notice their feed silently stopped importing.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds force: true to the create_table in an already-shipped, unrelated top_topics migration — a change traceable to no requirement in this PR. Any database that reaches this migration with a top_topics table already present (restored backups, environments that created the table out-of-band) silently drops the table and its data instead of failing loudly, and the data-drop semantics ride into production hidden inside an embed feature PR where no reviewer is looking for them.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined and never called anywhere in the diff, so the conditional-fetch design it implies shipped half-finished. Every hourly run re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed with no modified-since short-circuit, and the dead method tells maintainers that change detection exists when it does not; the deletion test removes all three lines.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls rewrites only a[href] and img[src] values that start with a single slash, so protocol-relative (//cdn.host/img.png) and bare-relative (images/img.png) URLs pass through untouched despite the method's stated contract to convert any relative URL to absolute. Embedded articles from feeds using those common URL styles render broken images and dead links inside the embed iframe and on the imported topic, and the next reader of the method gets no signal that two relative-URL forms were knowingly excluded.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact origin equality. Any origin that is a string prefix of the forum URL — e.g. a site registered at eviltrout.co when discourseUrl is http://eviltrout.com — passes the check and can drive discourse-resize messages, letting third-party content on the embedding page collapse or blow out the comments iframe height.

[ADVISORY] invalid_host? validates only the host of the original embed_url, but the actual fetch in TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url), which follows HTTP redirects, so the only-fetch-from-embeddable-host invariant is not enforced end-to-end. A compromised or MitM'd embeddable host (the check happily accepts plain http URLs) can 302 Discourse at any internal URL and have the response body imported and rendered, handing the trusted-but-external host a server-side fetch primitive the validation code visibly claims it does not have.

[ADVISORY] The embed layout loads stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but nothing in the diff adds embed.css (or embed.js) to the asset precompile list Rails requires for non-manifest assets. In production the compiled embed page requests /assets/embed-*.css and gets a 404, so every embedded comment widget renders unstyled — a failure invisible in development where all assets are served on demand.

[BUG] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes the entire scheduled PollFeed job synchronously (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) fetches the whole feed and imports every item) on the per-embed-request path, and any exception it raises propagates out before fetch_http can run. Each distinct embed URL's first view triggers a full feed fetch plus topic creation for every feed item (a blog with N articles gets N full polls inside their per-URL 60-second throttle windows), and one bad feed item or failed fetch leaves every embed URL permanently stuck on the loading page — the exception aborts perform_retrieve before fetch_http, RetrieveTopic retries under its own policy (bypassing PollFeed's retry:false), and the layering means a scheduled bulk job is now a synchronous dependency of the request path.

[BUG] The embed_url join key is written by two independent producers — PollFeed stores the feed item's link while TopicRetriever stores the page's discourseEmbedUrl query param — and every lookup (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) here and topic_id_for_embed at line 78) is exact string equality with no canonicalization of scheme, host case, www, trailing slash, or query string. When the feed's link differs from the URL the blog puts in discourseEmbedUrl (http vs https, trailing slash, www vs bare, WordPress ?p=123 vs pretty permalink), the lookup misses, fetch_http imports the article a second time, and one article ends up with two topics and two TopicEmbed rows — visitors comment on the retriever-created topic while the hourly poll keeps revising the feed-keyed one, splitting the discussion permanently.

[BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item error isolation, so the first item that raises — a missing title making PostCreator/TopicEmbed.create! fail on a NOT NULL column, a nil link, or ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the check-then-insert in TopicEmbed.import when the scheduled poll and a retriever-triggered poll run concurrently — aborts the entire loop. One malformed feed entry stops import of every remaining feed item until it ages out of the feed, and because TopicRetriever invokes this poll synchronously the same exception also kills retrieval for every embed URL, leaving those pages reloading the loading view forever.

[BUG] poll_feed reads only the Atom-style item element i.content, but RSS 2.0 feeds — the format the setting name advertises — expose body text as description (namespaced content:encoded is exposed by simple-rss as content_encoded), so i.content is nil/undefined and i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on the first item. Every hourly poll of an RSS 2.0 feed crashes before importing a single item, and via TopicRetriever's synchronous invocation the same crash blocks HTTP retrieval for all embed URLs — feed importing silently never works for the most common feed format while appearing enabled.

[BUG] TopicEmbed has no lifecycle coupling to its topic or post — no dependent: :destroy, no foreign keys in the create_topic_embeds migration, and Topic destruction knows nothing of topic_embeds — so deleting an imported topic or post leaves the topic_embeds row behind with a dangling topic_id. topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id so embed/best raises RecordNotFound (a 500) for that URL forever, TopicRetriever's exists? guard at topic_retriever.rb:37 treats the orphan row as a live embed so the article is never re-imported, and the update path crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) once embed.post is gone.

[BUG] The raw_html sanitization contract is enforced by only one of TopicEmbed.import's two callers — import_remote whitelists markup through Readability's tags/attributes options, while PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight into import where Post#cook returns it verbatim as cooked. Whatever markup the feed carries — script, iframe, on* event handlers — is stored as the post's cooked HTML and rendered unescaped to every reader on the Discourse origin, so any feed author (or feed hijacker) bypasses the whitelist the other path establishes and executes script in readers' browsers.

[BUG] The referer gate compares URI(request.referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host with case-sensitive verbatim string inequality and no scheme/port/www normalization, while embeddable_host is a free-form string setting with no validation. An admin who enters 'http://eviltrout.com', 'EvilTrout.com', 'eviltrout.com/', or who serves the blog under www. gets every embed request rejected with InvalidAccess — the whole feature is silently dead and the only diagnostic is 403s in logs.

[BUG] invalid_host? repeats the same unnormalized comparison (SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host), so any case/scheme/www divergence between the setting and the embed_url the blog's template emits makes the retriever refuse the URL. The URL is never imported and the embed page reloads the loading view every 30 seconds indefinitely, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic jobs that always no-op — a permanent 'Loading Discussion...' widget driven by a one-character configuration mismatch.

[BUG] absolutize_urls treats every href/src beginning with '/' as a root-relative path, but protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/img.jpg also match, and href.sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes before prepending the embedding host. Protocol-relative URLs — common in feed content — are rewritten to broken same-host paths like http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg, so images and links in imported articles that use the // form 404 for every reader.

[BUG] The disqus import now routes every thread through TopicEmbed.import_remote, which live-fetches each thread's page over HTTP, while the same change deletes the category option and the created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) fidelity from the old PostCreator call. Operators running the previously-shipped import with -c now hit Thor's unknown-option error, every imported topic is stamped with the import time instead of the Disqus thread's date, and an N-thread import performs N live HTTP fetches with no error handling — one unreachable page kills the whole import halfway, where the old path used only local XML data.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a feed-modified:<sha1> cache key that no code in this change ever reads — the conditional-fetch design it implies was dropped. Every hourly poll re-fetches and re-parses the full feed with no If-Modified-Since/ETag support, so operators of large feeds pay full transfer every hour, and maintainers reading the method reasonably believe change-detection caching exists when it does not.

[ADVISORY] The miss path enqueues RetrieveTopic with the raw unvalidated embed_url on every request (the only embed_url host/length validation lives inside the job) and the loading view reloads every 30 seconds, so a URL that can never be imported loops forever with no failure terminal state or negative-result caching. Readers of a misconfigured or unreachable embed see 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely while their browsers re-enqueue a Sidekiq job every 30 seconds each — a popular page with a broken embed becomes steady job-queue load, and arbitrarily long embed_url strings flow into job args bounded only by the in-job URI parse.

[ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? seeds the per-URL throttle with $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire — a non-atomic pair. A process kill or redis error between the two calls leaves retrieved:<url> with no TTL, so that URL is throttled forever, retrieval silently never runs again, and the page shows the loading view permanently; a single SET key 1 NX EX 60 closes it.

[ADVISORY] The update path revises only the post's raw content — the feed item's title is never passed to the revisor and nothing updates the topic title — so title changes in the feed never propagate. An article renamed after import keeps its stale title on the forum forever while its content silently updates, leaving the topic list disagreeing with the source until an editor discovers title updates were never wired.

[BUG] Line 6's `<%- end if %>` emits the Ruby fragment `end if`, which is a syntax error (a bare `end` cannot carry a modifier `if`), so this ERB template never compiles. Every request to /embed/best for a URL that already has a topic raises ActionView::Template::Error and returns a 500 — the feature's entire 'show the best comments' output path is dead and the iframe renders an error page instead of the discussion; the new controller specs cannot catch it because rspec-rails 2.x controller specs do not compile views (no render_views).

[BUG] cook returns raw unfiltered for cook_method raw_html, and the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import) never passes content through readability's tag whitelist — that whitelist exists only in import_remote — so third-party feed HTML is stored as cooked with zero sanitization. A malicious or MITM-compromised feed (open() happily fetches plain http) stores <script>/<iframe>/onerror payloads that render verbatim via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and in normal Discourse topic views — stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin and every embedding page with viewers' sessions; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb even asserts cooked == raw, codifying the unsanitized behavior as accepted without any security sign-off.

[BUG] import interpolates the unescaped url into both the href attribute and the link text of the 'Imported from' footer, and the only validation is the `^https?://` prefix regex, so a url like `http://x/<script>alert(1)</script>` or `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` passes and is stored as live HTML. Feed-controlled link values (i.link / i.id in poll_feed) and disqus export links inject script tags and event-handler attributes into imported posts, giving stored XSS wherever cooked is rendered raw — the PR's stated 'URL validation' objective checks the scheme but not the characters that matter for HTML injection.

[BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read with no rescue and no HTTP status handling, so a 404, timeout, or connection failure raises OpenURI::HTTPError/Errno::* straight out of the import. In the rewired disqus.thor import the exception aborts the entire migration mid-loop (the old code never fetched the link), leaving a half-imported forum; via TopicRetriever it kills the RetrieveTopic job, so the embed for that URL never appears while the loading view reloads forever.

[BUG] The diff deletes the documented `-c/--category` method_option from the Disqus importer, and the replacement TopicEmbed.import_remote path has no way to target a category — an accepted feature of an existing, unrelated tool removed with nothing in the embed objective justifying it. Operators rerunning the documented import command with -c can no longer file threads into their chosen category — every imported thread lands in uncategorized, silently mis-organizing migrated forums that previously used the option.

[BUG] topic_id_for_embed matches embed_url by exact string comparison and no path in the diff canonicalizes URLs (scheme, www prefix, trailing slash, query string), so a feed <link> that differs from the browser's page URL in any way misses the feed-imported topic. TopicRetriever then scrapes the page and creates a second topic for the same article — the embed binds to the empty scraped duplicate while the hourly PollFeed keeps updating the original as an orphan in the topic list; http-vs-https and tracking-query drift make this a routine case, defeating the PR's stated URL-handling objective.

[BUG] The layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JS string literal with no JavaScript escaping (the era's erubis/ERB::Util html_escape does not escape single quotes), so a referer whose host matches embeddable_host but whose query string contains `');…//` breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JS. An attacker lures a viewer to a legitimate embedding article with an appended query string like ?x=');alert(1);// — the iframe request carries that referer past the host check, and the injected JS executes on the Discourse origin with the viewer's session cookies.

[BUG] TopicEmbed has no dependent-destroy linkage to its post/topic, so deleting an embedded topic leaves an orphan row whose nil post is handed to PostRevisor.new(post) on the next content change, raising NoMethodError on nil. One staff-deleted embedded topic whose article later changes kills the hourly PollFeed job (sidekiq_options retry: false) every run — every feed item after the poisoned one stops importing permanently, and TopicRetriever's inline PollFeed call fails the same way, with no alerting path.

[BUG] ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is regenerated, leaving the default stack's committed lockfile (the very lock the _rails4 suffix implies exists) without either gem. Environments provisioning from the stale default lock never install the gems, so `require 'ruby-readability'` in TopicEmbed.import_remote and `require 'simple-rss'` in PollFeed raise LoadError at runtime, and frozen/deployment-mode bundle installs fail outright on the default stack.

[BUG] The rewrite replaces PostCreator's `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which never passes a timestamp, so every imported Disqus thread is dated at import-run time. Re-imported forums lose their original chronology — topics sort as if they were all created the day of the import — a silent regression of the importer's previously accepted data-fidelity behavior with no human sign-off for changing it.

[BUG] The PR adds `force: true` to create_table in an unrelated, already-committed migration, converting it into DROP TABLE + CREATE. Any database that reaches this migration with top_topics already populated (a dump restored without schema_migrations, or a parallel branch's table) silently loses its computed top-topic data, and this out-of-scope destructive edit to a shipped migration is invisible in the PR's stated embed objective.

[BUG] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative because `//cdn.host/x` starts with '/', and `sub(/^/+/, '')` strips both slashes, rewriting the URL to `prefix + '/cdn.host/x'`. Imported articles containing protocol-relative links or CDN image srcs get every such URL mangled into a nonexistent path on the embeddable host — broken images and links across all embedded posts, silently.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a 'feed-modified' redis key that no code in the diff ever reads — the incremental skip-unchanged-feed behavior its existence implies was silently dropped from the iteration. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into the imported_from footer (single-quoted href and bare text node) even though the only validation is the ^https?:// prefix check, so quotes and angle brackets pass through. A feed item link such as http://host/1'><script>alert(1)</script> injects markup into every rendered copy of the post (cooked is emitted raw), giving the feed author a second, independent stored-XSS path into the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the footer is built by interpolating the unescaped `url` into HTML: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`, with only a `/^https?:\/\//` prefix check. This allows quotes/angle brackets in `url` (e.g. `http://host/1'>`) to break out of the single-quoted href and inject markup. The created post is explicitly marked `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that mode, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so the injected HTML would be stored and rendered without sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed dereferences i.content with no nil guard, but items in description-only RSS 2.0 feeds — the format the feed_polling_url setting explicitly advertises — have no content element, so SimpleRSS yields nil and the poll crashes with NoMethodError. The hourly poll dies before importing anything, and because the job declares sidekiq_options retry: false the exception is discarded silently, so feed importing stops with no error surfaced to the operator.

Operators whose import scripts pass -c now fail (Thor rejects the unknown option) and every imported topic lands in uncategorized with today's timestamp instead of the thread's original date; a single dead link in the export raises OpenURI::HTTPError inside the threads loop and aborts the whole import mid-run with no resume — none of which the embed requirement asks for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the code that mapped `options[:category]` to a `category_id`, so existing scripts passing `-c/--category` will now fail option parsing and imported topics can no longer be routed to a chosen category. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view reloads the iframe unconditionally every 30 seconds with no retry cap and no error state, while the retrieval it waits on can fail permanently (embed_by_username blank, embed_url host differing from embeddable_host, fetch errors). A misconfigured embed — the most likely first-run state — shows visitors an eternal 'Loading Discussion...' widget that re-requests /embed/best and re-enqueues a RetrieveTopic job every 30 seconds per visitor, with nothing at the point of failure telling the operator why.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)`) with no retry limit or error handling. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil, it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`, so every reload triggers another enqueue. The retrieval path can permanently no-op without creating an embed (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true when `URI(@embed_url).host` differs from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, or `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when no user exists for `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase`), resulting in an endless loading widget plus repeated `/embed/best` requests and job enqueues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referer host check is the only gate on the unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint, but Referer is a client-supplied header, and the Jobs.enqueue at line 15 runs on every request with no request-level rate limit. Anyone can curl the endpoint with a forged Referer and unlimited distinct embed_url values to flood the sidekiq queue with RetrieveTopic jobs, each performing redis operations and — once past the per-URL 60-second key — an outbound HTTP fetch against the configured host, turning the forum into an unauthenticated job-flooding and request-amplification vector.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `GET /embed/best` endpoint (`routes.rb`) that only gates access via `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`). Since `Referer` is a client-supplied header, it can be forged, and the action does not require authentication (uses `current_user.try(:id)` but no login filter is shown). When no embed exists, it enqueues a Sidekiq job on every request (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)`), and the per-URL throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is defeated by supplying unlimited distinct `embed_url` values. For valid-host URLs, the job can proceed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `open(url)` outbound fetch, making this a real unauthenticated job-flooding / amplification DoS vector introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new specs cover only the settings gating and stub out the behavior the feature actually adds — poll_feed's URL fallback, entity unescaping and TopicEmbed.import call, plus TopicEmbed.import_remote and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/fetch_http, have zero coverage. A regression in the feed import loop (such as the nil-content crash or an escaping change) breaks feed importing with no failing spec, and because the job is scheduled with retry: false nothing in CI or production surfaces it until operators notice their feed silently stopped importing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing, link/id fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls) and in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/#fetch_http` plus `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (HTTP fetch + Readability). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds force: true to the create_table in an already-shipped, unrelated top_topics migration — a change traceable to no requirement in this PR. Any database that reaches this migration with a top_topics table already present (restored backups, environments that created the table out-of-band) silently drops the table and its data instead of failing loudly, and the data-drop semantics ride into production hidden inside an embed feature PR where no reviewer is looking for them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is defined and never called anywhere in the diff, so the conditional-fetch design it implies shipped half-finished. Every hourly run re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed with no modified-since short-circuit, and the dead method tells maintainers that change detection exists when it does not; the deletion test removes all three lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls rewrites only a[href] and img[src] values that start with a single slash, so protocol-relative (//cdn.host/img.png) and bare-relative (images/img.png) URLs pass through untouched despite the method's stated contract to convert any relative URL to absolute. Embedded articles from feeds using those common URL styles render broken images and dead links inside the embed iframe and on the imported topic, and the next reader of the method gets no signal that two relative-URL forms were knowingly excluded.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only `href`/`src` values with `start_with?('/')` are rewritten; bare-relative URLs like `images/img.png` are left unchanged despite the comment “Convert any relative URLs to absolute,” which can lead to broken links/images in imported content. Additionally, protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn...`) also match `start_with?('/')` and would be rewritten into `#{prefix}/cdn...`, which is incorrect for that common form. So the method’s behavior is incomplete/incorrect relative to its stated contract and can break embedded/imported rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact origin equality. Any origin that is a string prefix of the forum URL — e.g. a site registered at eviltrout.co when discourseUrl is http://eviltrout.com — passes the check and can drive discourse-resize messages, letting third-party content on the embedding page collapse or blow out the comments iframe height.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring containment check, not an exact-origin match. If `e.origin` is a prefix of `discourseUrl` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.co` vs `http://eviltrout.com`), `indexOf` returns 0 and the check passes, allowing a non-Discourse origin to send `discourse-resize` messages and control the iframe height.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalid_host? validates only the host of the original embed_url, but the actual fetch in TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url), which follows HTTP redirects, so the only-fetch-from-embeddable-host invariant is not enforced end-to-end. A compromised or MitM'd embeddable host (the check happily accepts plain http URLs) can 302 Discourse at any internal URL and have the response body imported and rendered, handing the trusted-but-external host a server-side fetch primitive the validation code visibly claims it does not have.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` the validation only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). But the actual fetch path `fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` uses `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and `open-uri` can follow HTTP redirects. That means an allowed external URL on the embeddable host can 30x-redirect Discourse to fetch content from a different host (potentially internal), violating the “only fetch from embeddable_host” intent and creating an SSRF primitive. The diff also explicitly accepts plain `http(s)` URLs via regex checks, so a MitM scenario is plausible given the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed layout loads stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but nothing in the diff adds embed.css (or embed.js) to the asset precompile list Rails requires for non-manifest assets. In production the compiled embed page requests /assets/embed-*.css and gets a 404, so every embedded comment widget renders unstyled — a failure invisible in development where all assets are served on demand.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new standalone stylesheet `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and a new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` that calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. The diff does not show `embed.css` being required by an existing manifest (e.g., `application.css`) or being added to any asset precompile allowlist/config. Under the default Rails asset pipeline behavior, non-manifest standalone CSS/JS files typically are not precompiled in production, so `/assets/embed-*.css` can 404 and the embed page would render unstyled. However, the diff does not include the app’s asset precompile configuration, so this is inferred from common defaults.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes the entire scheduled PollFeed job synchronously (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) fetches the whole feed and imports every item) on the per-embed-request path, and any exception it raises propagates out before fetch_http can run. Each distinct embed URL's first view triggers a full feed fetch plus topic creation for every feed item (a blog with N articles gets N full polls inside their per-URL 60-second throttle windows), and one bad feed item or failed fetch leaves every embed URL permanently stuck on the loading page — the exception aborts perform_retrieve before fetch_http, RetrieveTopic retries under its own policy (bypassing PollFeed's retry:false), and the layering means a scheduled bulk job is now a synchronous dependency of the request path.

adjudication.rationale:
In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before attempting `fetch_http` (and only then returns early if an embed was created). This is verifiable from:

```ruby
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end

fetch_http
```

Because this inline execution is not wrapped in any rescue, any exception from `Jobs::PollFeed` (e.g., `open-uri`/`SimpleRSS.parse` failures in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) will abort `perform_retrieve` and prevent `fetch_http` from ever running, even if HTTP retrieval could have worked. Also, `retrieved_recently?` throttles per `@embed_url`, so distinct embed URLs will each trigger a full feed poll/import when they first hit `perform_retrieve`, matching the finding's core behavior. The propagation of exceptions is a real functional failure mode introduced by wiring a bulk poll into this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed_url join key is written by two independent producers — PollFeed stores the feed item's link while TopicRetriever stores the page's discourseEmbedUrl query param — and every lookup (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) here and topic_id_for_embed at line 78) is exact string equality with no canonicalization of scheme, host case, www, trailing slash, or query string. When the feed's link differs from the URL the blog puts in discourseEmbedUrl (http vs https, trailing slash, www vs bare, WordPress ?p=123 vs pretty permalink), the lookup misses, fetch_http imports the article a second time, and one article ends up with two topics and two TopicEmbed rows — visitors comment on the retriever-created topic while the hourly poll keeps revising the feed-keyed one, splitting the discussion permanently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple paths that create/look up TopicEmbed rows keyed by exact-string `embed_url` without any normalization. `Jobs::PollFeed` calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` where `url` comes from `i.link`/`i.id` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), while `TopicRetriever` checks/creates based on `@embed_url` coming from the controller param (lib/topic_retriever.rb + app/controllers/embed_controller.rb) and `embed.js` constructs that param from the page’s `discourseEmbedUrl`. All lookups use `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first/exists?` and `topic_id_for_embed` uses `where(embed_url: embed_url)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), so any differences like http/https, host casing, www, trailing slash, or querystring will miss and can create a second topic/embed for the same article.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item error isolation, so the first item that raises — a missing title making PostCreator/TopicEmbed.create! fail on a NOT NULL column, a nil link, or ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the check-then-insert in TopicEmbed.import when the scheduled poll and a retriever-triggered poll run concurrently — aborts the entire loop. One malformed feed entry stops import of every remaining feed item until it ages out of the feed, and because TopicRetriever invokes this poll synchronously the same exception also kills retrieval for every embed URL, leaving those pages reloading the loading view forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code iterates `rss.items.each` and directly calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without any `rescue`/per-item isolation. Any exception raised while processing one item (e.g., from `TopicEmbed.import`/`PostCreator#create`/`TopicEmbed.create!` or a uniqueness violation on `topic_embeds.embed_url`) will abort the entire loop and fail the job. This is exacerbated by `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, so an exception in feed polling can also prevent embed retrieval from progressing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed reads only the Atom-style item element i.content, but RSS 2.0 feeds — the format the setting name advertises — expose body text as description (namespaced content:encoded is exposed by simple-rss as content_encoded), so i.content is nil/undefined and i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on the first item. Every hourly poll of an RSS 2.0 feed crashes before importing a single item, and via TopicRetriever's synchronous invocation the same crash blocks HTTP retrieval for all embed URLs — feed importing silently never works for the most common feed format while appearing enabled.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root bug: `poll_feed` assumes `i.content` exists, but many RSS 2.0 feeds provide item text via `description` (or `content_encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and calling `i.content.scrub` raises an exception. This aligns with the golden comment’s need for a fallback to `description` to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed has no lifecycle coupling to its topic or post — no dependent: :destroy, no foreign keys in the create_topic_embeds migration, and Topic destruction knows nothing of topic_embeds — so deleting an imported topic or post leaves the topic_embeds row behind with a dangling topic_id. topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id so embed/best raises RecordNotFound (a 500) for that URL forever, TopicRetriever's exists? guard at topic_retriever.rb:37 treats the orphan row as a live embed so the article is never re-imported, and the update path crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) once embed.post is gone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed` with `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` but no `dependent: :destroy` on either side, and the migration `create_topic_embeds` defines plain `topic_id`/`post_id` integers with no foreign keys. As a result, deleting a Topic or Post can leave orphan `topic_embeds` rows. This causes concrete failures shown by the added code paths: `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (pluck) and then `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, which will blow up if that topic_id no longer exists; `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so an orphan row prevents re-import; and `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post)` which will crash if `embed.post` is nil because the post was deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The raw_html sanitization contract is enforced by only one of TopicEmbed.import's two callers — import_remote whitelists markup through Readability's tags/attributes options, while PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight into import where Post#cook returns it verbatim as cooked. Whatever markup the feed carries — script, iframe, on* event handlers — is stored as the post's cooked HTML and rendered unescaped to every reader on the Discourse origin, so any feed author (or feed hijacker) bypasses the whitelist the other path establishes and executes script in readers' browsers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` constrains HTML via Readability tag/attribute whitelists, but `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly to `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) with no sanitization; `scrub` only addresses invalid encoding, not hostile tags/attributes. Therefore a feed item containing `<script>`, `<iframe>`, or `on*` handlers would be stored and served as cooked HTML, leading to XSS on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The referer gate compares URI(request.referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host with case-sensitive verbatim string inequality and no scheme/port/www normalization, while embeddable_host is a free-form string setting with no validation. An admin who enters 'http://eviltrout.com', 'EvilTrout.com', 'eviltrout.com/', or who serves the blog under www. gets every embed request rejected with InvalidAccess — the whole feature is silently dead and the only diagnostic is 403s in logs.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer gate does a strict string equality check: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is defined as a free-form string (site_settings.yml) and there’s no normalization/validation in the diff. If an admin enters values like `http://eviltrout.com`, `eviltrout.com/`, or `www.eviltrout.com`, the comparison will fail and every request will raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`, effectively breaking embedding. This broken behavior is directly implied by the diff’s comparison logic and settings definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] invalid_host? repeats the same unnormalized comparison (SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host), so any case/scheme/www divergence between the setting and the embed_url the blog's template emits makes the retriever refuse the URL. The URL is never imported and the embed page reloads the loading view every 30 seconds indefinitely, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic jobs that always no-op — a permanent 'Loading Discussion...' widget driven by a one-character configuration mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` the check is a strict string equality: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` (and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` similarly compares `URI(request.referer).host` to the setting). This could indeed reject an otherwise “same site” URL if the blog emits a different but related host (eg `www.` vs apex) or different casing, causing retrieval to never happen and leaving the iframe showing the `loading` view on reload. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls treats every href/src beginning with '/' as a root-relative path, but protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/img.jpg also match, and href.sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes before prepending the embedding host. Protocol-relative URLs — common in feed content — are rewritten to broken same-host paths like http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg, so images and links in imported articles that use the // form 404 for every reader.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the rewrite condition is `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` and the replacement uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` (same for `src`). Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` satisfy `start_with?('/')`, then `sub` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/img.jpg`, which is then rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.jpg` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`). This matches the finding and would break protocol-relative links/images in imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The disqus import now routes every thread through TopicEmbed.import_remote, which live-fetches each thread's page over HTTP, while the same change deletes the category option and the created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) fidelity from the old PostCreator call. Operators running the previously-shipped import with -c now hit Thor's unknown-option error, every imported topic is stamped with the import time instead of the Disqus thread's date, and an N-thread import performs N live HTTP fetches with no error handling — one unreachable page kills the whole import halfway, where the old path used only local XML data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus Thor import to stop using local XML thread data and instead call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), which does `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` with no rescue/handling (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is removed, so imported topics/posts will default to current time. Also the `--category/-c` Thor option is deleted, so operators using the previously-supported flag will now get an unknown option error. These are concrete, diff-grounded behavior breakages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key builds a feed-modified:<sha1> cache key that no code in this change ever reads — the conditional-fetch design it implies was dropped. Every hourly poll re-fetches and re-parses the full feed with no If-Modified-Since/ETag support, so operators of large feeds pay full transfer every hour, and maintainers reading the method reasonably believe change-detection caching exists when it does not.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `def feed_key` constructs a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1...}"`) but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or reads/writes any value keyed by it. `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no ETag/If-Modified-Since handling, so the presence of `feed_key` is misleading dead/incomplete functionality and implies change-detection caching that is not implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The miss path enqueues RetrieveTopic with the raw unvalidated embed_url on every request (the only embed_url host/length validation lives inside the job) and the loading view reloads every 30 seconds, so a URL that can never be imported loops forever with no failure terminal state or negative-result caching. Readers of a misconfigured or unreachable embed see 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely while their browsers re-enqueue a Sidekiq job every 30 seconds each — a popular page with a broken embed becomes steady job-queue load, and arbitrarily long embed_url strings flow into job args bounded only by the in-job URI parse.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` with only `params.require(:embed_url)` as validation, then renders `loading` (which auto-reloads every 30s in `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`). There is no controller-side throttling or negative-result caching, so an embed URL that can never be imported (misconfigured settings/unreachable URL/invalid host) will keep the user stuck on “Loading…” and re-enqueue a Sidekiq job every reload. The only guards are inside the job/retriever (`RetrieveTopic` only checks presence; `TopicRetriever` checks host and uses a 60s redis throttle *during execution*, not on enqueue), so unbounded/very long `embed_url` strings can also be pushed into job args repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? seeds the per-URL throttle with $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire — a non-atomic pair. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#invalid_host? compares only URI(embed_url).host to embeddable_host, ignoring scheme and port, so URLs like ftp://embeddable-host/x and http://embeddable-host:6379/ pass the check and are fetched by open() in TopicEmbed.import_remote (the fetch happens before import's https? regex discards the result). An anonymous attacker makes the Discourse server open connections to arbitrary ports (and FTP) on the embeddable host and publishes each HTTP response body as a visible topic, using the forum as a port-scanning and internal-service content-disclosure proxy against the embeddable host.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, invalid_host? only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, ignoring scheme and port. If the host matches, `perform_retrieve` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which does `open(url).read` with no scheme/port restriction. This allows requests like `ftp://<embeddable_host>/...` or `http://<embeddable_host>:<port>/...` to be fetched; for non-http(s) schemes the fetch still happens before `TopicEmbed.import` later rejects the URL, and for `http(s)` with arbitrary ports the content can proceed into import/publishing. This is a verifiable SSRF/port-scanning vector against the configured embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PostCreator assigns post.cook_method straight from @opts with no authorization guard anywhere in the diff, so any caller that forwards request-derived options into PostCreator lets the requester select the raw_html cook path and store arbitrary unsanitized HTML. If the posts endpoint passes client parameters into PostCreator opts (the same attribute-assignment pattern this line is added beside), any end user creates raw_html posts — unprivileged stored XSS sitewide; the privileged cook path ships with zero capability check at the sink.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new privileged rendering path (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`) and allows `PostCreator` to set `post.cook_method` directly from `@opts[:cook_method]` (`lib/post_creator.rb`). There is no authorization/capability check shown around selecting `:raw_html`, so this is a real, diff-grounded security footgun: any caller that passes user-influenced opts into `PostCreator` could inadvertently enable unsanitized HTML storage/serving. However, the finding’s claim that a specific request endpoint forwards client params into `PostCreator` is not verifiable from this diff alone, so the sitewide unprivileged XSS impact is plausible but not proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never asserts a 404 and never reaches params.require(:embed_url): with the default blank SiteSetting.embeddable_host (site_settings.yml ships embeddable_host: ''), the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises Discourse::InvalidAccess (403) before the action body runs, so the test passes via the host guard while the missing-param path it names has zero coverage. Deleting params.require(:embed_url) from EmbedController#best leaves this test green; a request without embed_url then flows into TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(nil) and enqueues a junk retrieve_topic job per request, while the suite reports the param guard as covered.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best` and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or referer host mismatches. In the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end`, nothing stubs `embeddable_host` (default in `site_settings.yml` is `''`, i.e. blank) nor sets a referer, so the request is rejected by `ensure_embeddable` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is evaluated. Therefore the test name implies missing-param coverage but actually only covers the embeddable host/referer guard. This is a real, diff-grounded testing/coverage issue, but not a functional defect in the shipped code since `params.require(:embed_url)` is present in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests pass for the wrong reason: SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is left at its default false and short-circuits the && chain in execute before the stubbed condition is ever evaluated (the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username stubs are dead code), so neither named guard is exercised. Removing the feed_polling_url.present? or embed_by_username.present? check from Jobs::PollFeed#execute keeps both tests green, letting the poller run with a blank feed URL (open(nil) raising every hour) or a blank username with no test failing.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is gated by `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples only stub `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username` to `nil`, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Given `config/site_settings.yml` sets `feed_polling_enabled: false` by default, the first condition likely short-circuits and those tests never actually exercise the `feed_polling_url.present?` / `embed_by_username.present?` guards. This is a real test coverage/verification problem, but the production code as shown still contains the guards, so it’s not itself a runtime defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test in the diff executes poll_feed's body — all four specs assert only delegation via expects(:poll_feed) — so the item-parsing logic is entirely unverified: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on RSS 2.0 items (SimpleRSS exposes description, not content, for RSS) and the 'url = i.id' Atom fallback branch is never triggered. The feature's primary import path crashes on the first item of a standard RSS 2.0 feed and, because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false, dies silently every hour while the suite stays green; a single spec parsing a real RSS fixture would have caught it.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, all examples only assert whether execute delegates to poll_feed (expects(:poll_feed)) and never exercise poll_feed itself, so the newly added parsing/import logic in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (SimpleRSS.parse, rss.items.each, url fallback to i.id, and CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) is entirely untested. The finding’s specific claim that SimpleRSS RSS2 items lack `content` (thus `i.content.scrub` would NoMethodError) is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone; what *is* verifiable is that this risk-bearing logic has no coverage and nil-safety is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every test in the file mocks perform_retrieve, and the two valid-host tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the redis setnx/expire throttle, the TopicEmbed-exists bail, the PollFeed delegation, fetch_http's user lookup, and TopicEmbed.import_remote (the readability extraction that is the feature's core fetch path) never execute under any test. An inverted or dropped throttle — the only rate limit on externally-triggered fetches — or a crash anywhere in the retrieve pipeline ships with a green suite; the first real embed request is the first time this code ever runs.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the first three examples assert perform_retrieve is never called, and in the “with a valid host” context the tests stub retrieved_recently? and only assert whether perform_retrieve is invoked. No test exercises TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, so the core pipeline shown in lib/topic_retriever.rb (TopicEmbed.exists? early return, optional Jobs::PollFeed execution, fetch_http user lookup, and TopicEmbed.import_remote) is not covered by these tests. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The success-path tests assert collaborator calls but never assert the response: neither asserts which template renders ('best' vs 'loading') and TopicRetriever.expects(:new) carries no argument constraint, so the embed_url forwarded through the job is unverified. A regression that renders 'loading' unconditionally (every embed shows the 30-second reload loop even when a topic exists) or forwards the wrong URL to the retriever keeps the suite green.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` under the "success" context, the tests mostly assert collaborator interactions (`TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`, `TopicView.expects(:new)`) and generic success headers, but they never assert which template/view is rendered (`best` vs `loading`). In particular, the "no previous embed" test doesn’t assert that `loading` was rendered, and the "topic_id is found" test doesn’t assert that `best` was rendered, so a regression that always renders `loading` could slip through as long as those collaborator expectations still occur. Also, `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` has no argument constraint, so it would not catch forwarding the wrong `embed_url` into the retriever/job path (the job ultimately calls `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], ...)`).
