adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) branch has no distinguishing test: the only spec in the diff that exercises PostRevisor with skip_validations (topic_embed_spec's update test) feeds it content that passes validation anyway, so reverting to a plain @post.save is indistinguishable. If the flag regresses, real RSS revisions that fail validation silently no-op while TopicEmbed.import still runs embed.update_column(:content_sha1) unconditionally, permanently discarding that article update on the next hourly poll — with no test failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and TopicEmbed.import’s update path calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only asserts the content changes, without any case that would fail under validations). So the new conditional validation behavior is effectively untested: the current specs won’t distinguish whether validations are skipped or not. The finding’s broader “data loss if validations fail” scenario depends on a future regression (since skip_validations is currently always passed on RSS updates), so it’s not a verifiable present defect from this diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern around newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test covers TopicEmbed.import's update branch when the embedded post no longer exists: nothing in the diff cleans up the topic_embeds row on post deletion, so embed.post returns nil and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError on @post.raw, yet the only update spec uses a live post. An admin deleting an imported post turns the next content-changing hourly PollFeed run into a permanent crash loop (retry: false, content_sha1 never advances past the raise), silently killing feed importing for the site while the suite stays green.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes `embed.post` is present: `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the referenced post has been deleted (no FK constraints shown; `topic_embeds.post_id` is just an integer with `null: false`, and no dependent-destroy/cleanup logic is added in this diff), `embed.post` can be `nil`, causing `PostRevisor` to later dereference `@post` and raise. `Jobs::PollFeed` calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a repeatable exception would break feed importing each run. The provided spec only covers updating when the post still exists, not the deleted-post edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'raises an error with a missing host' and 'raises an error with no referer' tests assert only response.should_not be_success, which cannot distinguish the intended Discourse::InvalidAccess 403 from an unrelated 500 crash, and no spec sends a malformed referer so the new rescue URI::InvalidURIError branch in ensure_embeddable is never triggered. If the guard regressed to raise an unhandled exception (or the rescue were dropped), requests with a malformed Referer would return a 500 crash page instead of a clean 403 and both tests would stay green.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the tests "raises an error with a missing host" and "raises an error with no referer" only assert `response.should_not be_success`, which would still pass for an unexpected 500 error and does not verify the intended Discourse::InvalidAccess handling/status. Also, EmbedController#ensure_embeddable rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` (triggered by a malformed `request.referer`), but the specs never stub a malformed referer value—only `nil` (which becomes `URI('')` and does not raise)—so that rescue branch is untested. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage/robustness issue rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test probes with plain text ('muhahaha new contents!'), so post.cooked =~ /new contents/ passes whether the revision re-cooks via the raw_html path or mangles the HTML through the regular markdown pipeline — the only spec covering the hourly PostRevisor path cannot detect a cook_method regression on revise. A change that resets cook_method or re-cooks imported posts as markdown on revision strips embedded article HTML on every feed update while the suite stays green.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, the update path (`TopicEmbed.import` when an embed already exists) exercises `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)`, but the assertion only checks `post.cooked =~ /new contents/` using plain text (`"muhahaha new contents!"`). It does not assert that `post.cook_method` remains `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` or that cooked output preserves HTML, so a regression where `cook_method` is reset or the revision path re-cooks via the regular pipeline could slip by while this spec still passes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shared be_success and X-Frame-Options assertions live in an after block instead of the example bodies, so they run even when an example fails before populating the response. Any failing example in the 'success' context (e.g., an unmet mock expectation) cascades into a second confusing failure on an unpopulated response, and no error-path example can ever be added inside the context without the teardown failing it spuriously.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the `context "success"` defines an `after` block that unconditionally asserts `response.should be_success` and `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'].should == "ALLOWALL"`. This teardown runs regardless of whether the example itself fails (e.g., due to unmet mock expectations) and also prevents adding any non-success/error-path examples within the same context because the `after` will fail them. These assertions belong in each example (or a shared example) rather than an unconditional `after`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The non-standard-port branch of absolutize_urls (prefix << ":#{uri.port}" unless port is 80/443) is never triggered by any test — topic_embed_spec only imports http://eviltrout.com/123, whose URI port is 80. A regression that drops or corrupts the port suffix for feeds served on :8080/:3000 produces dead absolute links in every imported post with no test failing.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix includes a non-standard port via `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. The added spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) only uses `url = 'http://eviltrout.com/123'`, which implies port 80, so the non-standard-port branch is not exercised by any test in this diff. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added edge-case logic (not a currently verifiable defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Adding force: true to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration makes any re-run of it execute DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics, silently destroying the existing table instead of failing loudly with 'table already exists'. In any environment where this migration re-executes against a populated top_topics table (schema_migrations out of sync after a restore, a manual db:migrate:redo, or a dev DB holding the table without the version row), all accumulated per-period topic metrics (view/like/post counts per period) are dropped with no backup and no rollback path; without force: true the same re-run would have aborted harmlessly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it. If this migration is ever re-executed against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, version tracking mismatch), it can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data instead of failing with "table already exists". This is a real, diff-grounded data-loss risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true bakes a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS into the migration, so once the table holds production data any re-run silently destroys the embed_url-to-topic mapping. After this ships, a re-run triggered by a schema_migrations/restore mismatch drops every topic_embeds row; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then returns nil for known URLs, so the next retrieve/poll re-imports each article and creates a duplicate topic while the original topic and its replies remain on the forum, doubling content until the mapping is manually rebuilt.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, which would destroy all `topic_embeds` rows if the migration is ever re-run against an environment where the table already exists. Since `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` relies on that table for URL→topic mapping, losing rows would break lookups and could lead to re-import/duplicate topic creation on subsequent retrieve/poll operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topic_embeds rows have no deletion lifecycle: topic_id and post_id are plain integers with no FK, and nothing in the diff destroys the TopicEmbed row when its topic or post is deleted, while the unique index on embed_url makes each mapping permanent. When staff delete an embedded topic, the topic_embeds row survives: EmbedController#best keeps resolving that embed_url to the deleted topic and renders it in the iframe, the next feed poll routes through the update path and revises the deleted topic's post via PostRevisor instead of creating a fresh topic, and the unique index prevents the URL from ever being re-embedded without manual SQL deletion of the stale row.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a persistent mapping table `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` as plain integers (migration `create_topic_embeds`), a unique index on `embed_url`, and model associations without any `dependent: ...` cleanup. Lookup paths (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` used by `EmbedController#best`) and update paths (`TopicEmbed.import` reuses `embed.post` and revises it) assume the referenced Topic/Post still exist. If a Topic or Post is deleted, nothing in this diff removes the `topic_embeds` row, so future requests/imports will continue to resolve via the stale row, and the unique index can prevent re-embedding the same URL without manual deletion. This is a concrete lifecycle/correctness problem evident from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs as site-relative: href.start_with?('/') matches '//host/path' and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes, rewriting //cdn.example.com/img.png into http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png. Every imported article containing protocol-relative links or images (common in RSS content from https sites) gets its URLs mangled into broken paths that are stored verbatim in the post via the raw_html cook method; because content_sha1 is computed on the pre-transformation source text, unchanged articles are never re-revised, so the corrupted URLs persist in stored data even after the transformation is fixed.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the condition `href.start_with?('/')` (and same for `src`) will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`. The rewrite then does `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, which strips both leading slashes and incorrectly turns `//cdn...` into `http://<embed-host>/cdn...`, mangling the URL. Separately, in TopicEmbed.import, `content_sha1` is computed from the unmodified `contents` before calling `absolutize_urls`; the stored post raw/cooked uses the transformed HTML. Therefore if the transform logic changes later (e.g., fixing this bug) but the feed content is unchanged, `content_sha1` will not change and the post will not be revised, leaving previously corrupted URLs persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten Disqus import drops the created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) argument the previous implementation passed, so TopicEmbed.import_remote creates every imported topic with the current timestamp instead of the original thread date. Anyone running the disqus import after this change gets an archive whose topics are all dated at import time; the chronological ordering of the imported discussions is destroyed and cannot be recovered without re-running the import against the original Disqus export.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the old implementation created the first post/topic with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The new code replaces this with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or pass through any `created_at` value to `PostCreator` (they only pass `title`, `raw`, `skip_validations`, `cook_method`). Therefore imported topics/posts will use the current timestamp rather than the original Disqus thread date, affecting chronological ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces a full posts-table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on every PostgreSQL version current at this time (the metadata-only ADD COLUMN default optimization only arrived in PG 11). Operators of large forums — Discourse's target market — hit a hard site-wide outage while db:migrate runs: every request touching posts blocks for the whole rewrite, which takes minutes on multi-million-row posts tables; adding the column nullable and backfilling/defaulting in a follow-up step would keep the table readable and writable during the deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions before the metadata-only default optimization (not shown/controlled in this diff), this pattern is well-known to require rewriting the whole table and taking an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock, which can cause a significant outage on large `posts` tables. This is an operational/availability concern with the migration approach rather than an application correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_url is created as varchar(255) while TopicEmbed guards it only with validates_presence_of, so any feed item whose link exceeds 255 characters fails TopicEmbed.create! with a PostgreSQL 'value too long for type character varying(255)' error inside the import transaction. A single long-URL item in the operator-configured RSS feed raises out of rss.items.each and aborts the entire poll (the job runs with sidekiq_options retry: false), so every item after it in the feed is never imported, and the poll crashes again on the same item each hour until it rotates out of the feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `t.string :embed_url` uses Rails’ default `varchar(255)` limit, and `TopicEmbed` only validates presence (no length constraint). `TopicEmbed.import` calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction with the provided URL; a URL >255 chars would raise a DB error. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without rescuing exceptions, so one long URL would abort the whole poll run. The job is scheduled hourly and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so it would keep failing on subsequent runs until the feed item changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed flow has no failure state: EmbedController#best fire-and-forgets the RetrieveTopic job and renders 'loading', and this view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds, so a permanently failed retrieval (unreachable article, Readability failure, or fetch_http's silent return when embed_by_username is unset or names a missing user — which is the default config, since site_settings.yml ships embed_by_username: '') leaves the visitor in an infinite 'Loading Discussion...' loop with no error ever surfaced. A blog reader on any article whose retrieval failed sees a perpetual loading spinner in the comments area; in the unset-username case the job even completes 'successfully' while doing nothing, so neither the visitor nor the operator gets any signal — the 30s reload just re-enqueues a throttled no-op job on every cycle.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil, then renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view unconditionally reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), causing an endless loop if retrieval never produces a TopicEmbed. Retrieval can permanently no-op: TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns if the configured user is missing (lib/topic_retriever.rb: `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first; return if user.blank?`), and the default setting ships as empty string (config/site_settings.yml: `embed_by_username: ''`). There is no error view/state surfaced, so visitors can be stuck in perpetual "Loading Discussion..." with repeated re-enqueue attempts (throttled to 60s by redis, but still no terminal state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] retrieved_recently? commits the 60-second throttle key via $redis.setnx before any work is performed and never clears it when perform_retrieve subsequently fails or no-ops, so retries of the failed retrieval are silently suppressed while the job reports success. After one failed fetch the URL is un-retrievable for 60s while the user watches the loading page — sidekiq retries of the raised job and jobs re-enqueued by the page's reload all bail at the throttle and 'succeed' without working; additionally setnx and expire are two separate round-trips, so a worker crash between them leaves 'retrieved:<url>' with no TTL and that embed URL is never retrieved again (permanent loading, zero errors).

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieve` gates work on `retrieved_recently?` (returns true => skips `perform_retrieve`). `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This means the throttle is committed *before* any retrieval work happens; if `perform_retrieve` later fails/raises (e.g., in `fetch_http` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), a Sidekiq retry will see the throttle key and skip work, causing the retry to complete successfully without doing the retrieval. Also, because `setnx` and `expire` are separate calls, a crash between them can leave the key without a TTL, permanently suppressing retrieval for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed iterates rss.items with no per-item error isolation while the job runs with sidekiq_options retry: false (line 13), so the first item lacking a content element — SimpleRSS returns nil for missing tags — raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub at line 36 and kills the run mid-loop, deterministically, on every hourly execution. Every item after the first content-less entry (common in RSS 2.0 feeds without content:encoded) is dropped forever — the importer stalls at the same item on every run with no retry, topics simply stop appearing, and the only evidence is a sidekiq failure entry; the same mechanism means any single bad item (nil title, PostCreator failure) permanently blocks all later feed items.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each RSS item. If `i.content` is `nil` (common when feeds lack a `content`/`content:encoded` element), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-iteration. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so that run will not be retried, and subsequent scheduled executions will deterministically fail again as long as the feed continues to include such an item, preventing later items from being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path uses embed.post unguarded even though topic_embeds has no dependent-destroy and survives deletion of its post, so when the article's content changes after the post was deleted, PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! crashes with NoMethodError on nil.raw inside should_revise?. A deleted post with a surviving TopicEmbed row turns the next content change into a NoMethodError that — inside PollFeed's retry:false run — stalls the feed at that item exactly like the content-less-item crash, and TopicEmbed.import can never recover for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` changes. If the associated post has been deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains (no `dependent: :destroy` / cascade is shown in this diff, and the migration only adds an index—no FK constraints), `embed.post` will be nil and `PostRevisor` will raise when it dereferences `@post` (e.g., in `should_revise?`). This would also abort `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` mid-iteration (and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the run won’t be retried).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import silently returns nil for any non-http(s) URL with no log and no error result, and PollFeed feeds it nil whenever an RSS item's link is missing or relative and the i.id fallback is nil for RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb:33-34), so those items vanish without a trace. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` deliberately and silently returns `nil` for any URL not matching `/^https?\:\/\//` (`return unless url =~ ...`), and there is even a spec asserting this behavior (`returns nil when the URL is malformed`). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, `url` is set from `i.link` and then possibly replaced by `i.id` when blank/invalid; if both are blank/nil (or `i.id` is still non-http/relative), `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` will be called with `nil`/invalid and will silently no-op with no logging. That’s a real, diff-grounded observability/edge-case issue (items can be dropped without any trace), but it’s not clearly a defect since the silent-nil behavior is intentional per the added test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed silently returns when embed_by_username names no existing user — execute() only checks the setting is present, not that the user exists — so a typo'd, renamed, or deleted username makes the scheduled job complete 'successfully' every hour while importing nothing. An admin with a misconfigured username runs a feed importer that reports success and creates zero topics, with no log line to reveal the cause.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows Jobs::PollFeed#execute only guards on SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?/feed_polling_url/embed_by_username presence, but Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed then does `user = User.where(username_lower: ...).first` and immediately `return if user.blank?` with no logging/exception. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is defined but never called anywhere — the conditional-fetch bookkeeping its name and SHA1-of-feed-URL imply was never wired up, so every hourly run re-fetches and re-processes the entire feed while the dead method advertises modification tracking that does not exist. The next maintainer adding If-Modified-Since support will assume feed state is already persisted; meanwhile every poll pays the full-feed fetch and per-item import cost (the content_sha1 dedup only prevents duplicate writes, not the repeated work).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computing a Redis key from SHA1 of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff. The polling implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` inside `poll_feed`, with no use of `feed_key` or any stored “last modified”/etag state, so each hourly run will re-fetch and iterate all items. While `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes writes via `content_sha1`, the repeated fetch/parse/per-item work is still done, and the presence of an unused `feed_key` suggests incomplete modification-tracking wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote buffers the entire remote article with open(url).read — no size cap and no explicit timeout — before Readability parses it, on a sidekiq worker reached from every novel embed_url page view. A huge or slow page on the admin-configured embeddable_host balloons worker memory or pins the worker for open-uri's full default 60-second read window per attempt, degrading the shared sidekiq queue for everyone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` (lib/topic_embed.rb) and then passes the full string to `Readability::Document`. There is no explicit timeout, streaming, or size limit in this method. This is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` enqueued by `EmbedController#best` on a novel `embed_url` page view, so a large/slow page on the configured `embeddable_host` can tie up a Sidekiq worker and allocate unbounded memory. That’s a real availability/security defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed fetches the feed with open() and then iterates rss.items with no count cap, running PostCreator (which enqueues per-post processing jobs) for every item in a single job. A feed with thousands of entries becomes one multi-hour job that floods the sidekiq queue with per-post jobs and mints thousands of topics in one poll — no bound exists anywhere on this path.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then unconditionally iterates `rss.items.each` with no limit/backoff. Each item calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, which for new URLs wraps a `PostCreator.new(...).create` inside a transaction and can therefore create a topic/post per feed entry in a single scheduled job run. The diff shows no cap on item count, pagination, or time budget, so a large feed can cause an excessively long-running job and create an unbounded number of topics in one poll.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every request to /embed/best for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no rate limit on the endpoint, and the per-URL 60s throttle inside the job is keyed on the full URL, so varying the path or query string bypasses it — each novel URL triggers a full HTTP fetch of the embeddable_host page and, on success, creation of a real topic. An anonymous client forging a Referer header can flood the sidekiq queue, pin workers on outbound fetches against the embedded site, and mint unbounded scraped topics in the forum's database, exhausting workers and storage on the request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `/embed/best` which, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` with no controller-side throttling (`EmbedController#best`). The only throttle is in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which keys Redis on the full URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying path/query produces a new key and bypasses the 60s limit. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` then calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` and can create a new topic/post/embed record for each novel URL on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` host equality, which is client-controllable, so an anonymous client can trigger unbounded job enqueues/outbound fetches/topic creation. This is a verifiable resource-exhaustion/spam vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs the entire scheduled PollFeed job inline (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) with no lock, so it routinely overlaps the hourly scheduled instance or another embed view's inline run; both pass the TopicEmbed.exists? check and create duplicate topics until one hits the unique index. Concurrent runs produce duplicate full-feed fetches and ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique failures from TopicEmbed.create! that roll back the topic while PostCreator's already-enqueued post-processing jobs reference the rolled-back post IDs, leaving recurring failed-job noise and wasted worker time.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, the code runs the scheduled feed poller inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) with no locking/throttling beyond the per-`@embed_url` redis key, while `PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates the whole feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic "check then create" (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction) with only a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` as protection. Concurrent runs (scheduled hourly job plus inline runs, or multiple inline runs) can therefore race and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` from `create!` for the same `embed_url`, causing avoidable failures/noise and duplicated full-feed fetch work.
